newsitem.title: RWANDA: WFP says food aid critical in Rwanda in short-term.
newsitem.headline: WFP says food aid critical in Rwanda in short-term.

text.p: The U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) said on Tuesday food aid would be critical for Rwanda in coming months as it absorbed 500,000 refugees returned from eastern Zaire.
It said food aid was the primary source for all returnees and would continue to be so until the next agricultural season, starting in January and with crops being harvested in July.

"The sudden return of hundreds of thousands of refugees will require a dramatic expansion of WFP food activities, if returnees are to be successfully reintegrated into their home communes and prepared for the next planting season," it said.

"WFP officials predict that with the return of more people to Rwanda, food production should gradually begin to increase in the long term but it is clear food aid will be critical over the coming months with more people trying to get access to even less food," it added.

The WFP statement quoted a report from Famine Early Warning Systems estimating that Rwanda's current harvest due in January would not be as large as last year's, which was 20 percent below levels before the country's 1994 civil war and genocide.
It said a dry spell in October had in particular disrupted production of beans, a staple food in Rwanda, and the crop was expected to be 30 percent below the previous season's average.
WFP said more than 250,000 returnees in their home communes had received their relief food packages in the last five days.
